content: The guidance will undergo review and revision in 2015 to develop comprehensive implementation guidelines for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), incorporating the experiences gained from its application in various countries. Until then, emerging scientific evidence related to PrEP will be continuously monitored. If new evidence arises before 2015 that necessitates changes to the current guidance, such revisions will be promptly undertaken and communicated directly to the relevant countries. This guidance is available in English, French, and Spanish. It is being distributed to countries and to WHO and UNAIDS country staff, who will be requested to support, as needed, the development of demonstration project research based on this guidance. All members of the Guidelines Development Group and the External Review Group were required to complete a WHO declaration of interests form. Four individuals disclosed potential conflicts of interest. One panel member, Carlos Caceres, had received travel support from an institution involved in one of the key studies reviewed. However, as no personal benefit would result from his involvement in this guidance, this was not considered a conflict of interest. An external peer reviewer, Lynn Paxton, disclosed that Gilead Sciences, the manufacturer of the drugs reviewed in this guidance, had provided drugs to her institution for a study conducted in Botswana. Since Dr. Paxton did not personally benefit from this, the Steering Group determined that no conflict of interest existed. Two other individuals reported professional responsibilities related to PrEP, but the Steering Group concluded that these did not constitute conflicts of interest. The references cited include key studies and reviews on PrEP and HIV prevention strategies, such as: 1. Abdool Karim SS et al. (2011) on drug concentrations after topical and oral antiretroviral PrEP and implications for HIV prevention in women. 2. Padian NS et al. Thigpen MC et al. on antiretroviral PrEP for heterosexual HIV transmission in Botswana. 7. Peterson L et al. (2007) on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for HIV prevention in women. 8. Van Damme L et al. on PrEP for HIV infection among African women. 9. Donnell D et al. on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate drug levels and their correlation with HIV-1 protective effects in Kenya and Uganda. 10. Abdool Karim Q et al. (2010) on the effectiveness and safety of tenofovir gel as an antiretroviral microbicide for HIV prevention in women. 11. Celum C et al. on acyclovir and HIV-1 transmission in individuals co-infected with HIV-1 and HSV-2. 16. WHO guidelines on HIV and STI prevention and treatment among men who have sex with men and transgender individuals. 17. Paltiel AD et al. on the impact of PrEP in the United States on lifetime infection risk, clinical outcomes, and cost-effectiveness.
